propositions: Prompt cache is written on every plan-review gate call but never read across calls, paying premium write rates with zero inter-call benefit.

The marked cache prefix embeds the full plan text by design, making it unique per ticket and unsuitable for cross-ticket reuse, but preventing within-run verifier-to-verifier reads because the breakpoint sits after pass-specific stance suffixes instead of at the shared-prefix boundary.

Single-turn plan-review passes (finder, verifier, prereq-verifier, coach, ticket-digest) each generate a distinct system prompt, so even within one run no cross-pass cache read occurs despite shared leading bytes.

The cache efficiency diagnostic (warn_if_cache_ineffective) detects only write==0 AND read==0, missing the write-every-call/read-never-anywhere shape that wastes premium tokens on single-chunk leaf reviews.

Relocating the cache breakpoint to the end of the byte-stable shared_plan_prefix (via dynamic instructions) allows the finder write to be read by pass-2 verifiers within one run and by same-ticket re-reviews within the TTL.

Cross-ticket prefix identity is unsatisfiable without evicting the plan from the marked prefix, which would destroy within-run container and chunk warm-then-fan-out reuse that demonstrably works (multi-step code reviews achieve cache_read >> 0).
